purpose: Ergotamine is used to treat migraine headaches and cluster headaches. It works best when taken at the very first sign of a headache coming on. It is not used to prevent headaches, only to stop them once they start.
how_it_works: When you get a migraine, certain blood vessels in your head widen and cause pain. Ergotamine works by squeezing or narrowing those blood vessels back down, which helps relieve the throbbing pain. Think of it like gently tightening a garden hose that was letting too much water through.
common_side_effects: Nausea and vomiting are the most common side effects. You may also feel tingling or numbness in your fingers or toes, dizziness, or mild muscle cramps. Some people feel weakness in their legs.
warnings: Do not take this medicine too often — using it more than a couple of times a week can actually cause more headaches, called rebound headaches. Do NOT use it if you are pregnant, have heart disease, high blood pressure, liver or kidney problems, or circulation problems. Never combine it with certain antibiotics like erythromycin or antifungal medicines, as this can cause a dangerous reaction. Seek help immediately if you have chest pain, very cold or blue fingers, or severe leg cramps after taking it.
typical_dosing: The usual starting dose is 1 to 2 milligrams at the first sign of a migraine, taken under the tongue or by mouth. You may take another dose every 30 minutes if needed, but do not take more than 6 mg in a single attack or more than 10 mg in one week. Always follow your doctor's exact instructions.
